description: Authentication does not authenticate. An account that exists signs in with any password at all, including an empty one, because verifyPassword receives the password and never compares it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded success responses in production code
required_outcomes.why: login() returns `status: 200` on the success branch, and the success branch is reached for every password.

required_outcomes.title: project contains fake email addresses or domains in production code
required_outcomes.why: the accounts people sign in as are placeholder addresses at an example domain, so the whole account table is a stand-in.

required_outcomes.title: project contains TODO or FIXME comments in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `TODO` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what the marker is on — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the TODO is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/demo-analytics/scenario.json` requires `should_fix_first` for `CandidateCategory::Todo` at `src/analytics.js` and this fixture requires `must_fix` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `noop_heuristics`, which read the login branch that returns success for every password.

required_outcomes.why: the author left a TODO on the exact line that would have compared the password, and shipped anyway.

required_outcomes.title: project contains mock usage in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads `mock` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`. What this fixture is about is the mock account table standing in for a real user store, and that is what the scanner does not read.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a reading of what the mock stands in for — a store of real accounts, a password comparison — which would make `GapKind::SubstitutedAction` reachable for this outcome rather than `UnfinishedMarker`. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `noop_heuristics`, which read the login branch that returns success for every password.

required_outcomes.why: the production account table is named mock_users.

required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the marker is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/dead-button/scenario.json` requires `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Placeholder` at `public/app.js` and `fixtures/adversarial/demo-analytics/scenario.json` requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. required_outcomes.why: the credentials in the account table are described in the source as placeholders.
these candidates are about a sign-in path a real user walks through, so they must not be filed as style noise.

forbidden_outcomes.description: Sign-in is reported as working, secure, verified or passing. Any password opens an existing account.
The project aggregates to green while authentication has not been shown to reject a wrong password.
The fixture's own `npm test` exit code is accepted as evidence that sign-in is safe.
The always-true password check, the placeholder accounts and the TODO are not reported at all.

notes: Coverage gap, recorded rather than hidden: SURE still has no detector that reads an always-true password comparison as such. The scan fires on what surrounds it — a hard-coded success status on the login branch, placeholder accounts, a TODO on the line that would have compared the password, and a production table named mock_users. A grader must not read 'fake-auth fired' as 'SURE understands password verification'. Severity, recorded rather than measured here: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires must_fix for this case, and must_fix is what noop_heuristics reaches for the two rows it fires on — the hard-coded success on the login branch and the placeholder accounts, both MustFix, critical = false, EvidenceClass::Inference. The three candidate_scanner outcomes land at can_fix_later, because that scanner reads a `TODO`, a `mock` or a `placeholder` as an unfinished marker and not as a password comparison that was never made; each says so in its own `required_severity_unmet` block, which carries the reason the requirement stands unmet and what would have to change for it to be met. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these five proposals and names the coverage gap in its own test name and comment, and its every_recorded_detector_severity_is_what_the_detector_produces_today reads this file's own detector_severity_today values and runs the detector named beside each one. Before P7-T011 every scanner here emitted Severity::Note, so none of these weights was reachable; that the required and the delivered severity were once different is kept as SEVERITY_BEFORE_P7T011 in that file and in git, and the test that recorded the gap was inverted rather than deleted: it is what_is_detected_now_carries_the_weight_the_manifest_requires now, and it asserts the severity the manifest requires rather than the gap.
